title: Add NVTX ranges, runtime counters, microbench harness and perf dashboard
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Improve visibility into runtime hotspots for kernel launches, scheduler latency, KV-cache behavior and continuous batching. This PR introduces NVTX ranges around key runtime paths, lightweight counters for KV cache hits/misses and batch formation, a microbench harness for per-op latency measurements, and a Grafana/Prometheus dashboard + ingestion helper to make these signals actionable.

What changed (high-level):
- Add NVTX annotations around GPU kernel launches, dispatcher/scheduler queues, KV cache lookups and cache population paths.
- Introduce atomic runtime counters exposed via /metrics for: kvcache_hits, kvcache_misses, batch_formed_count, batch_flush_latency_ms_histogram, scheduler_queue_wait_ms_histogram.
- Microbench harness (tools/microbench) that runs synthetic workloads against the runtime to capture p50/p95/p99 for kernel launches, KV cache hit/miss penalties, and batching behavior. Harness supports CPU/GPU modes and a minimal YAML-driven scenario definition.
- Perf dashboard: grafana/dashboard/json + prometheus scrape config and ingestion helper (scripts/telemetry/ingest_metrics.py) to populate a long-running perf dashboard used by SRE and runtime owners.
- Add ci job microbench-smoke that runs a short harness with mocked models to detect regressions in end-to-end latency on PRs.

Testing: Unit tests for counter registration and NVTX guards added. Microbench CI runs a 30s smoke on linux-gpu runner (mocked). Manual validation performed on benchmark-lab: compared before/after for a continuous-batching workload (20% median improvement in scheduler queue wait after small scheduler change).

Backward compatibility: All instrumentation is optional behind runtime flag --telemetry-enabled (default off for production until rollout). NVTX and counters are no-ops when disabled.

Related: Linear ENG-2314, ENG-2419. See benchmark-lab run IDs attached in review comments.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of NVTX scopes (no heavy allocations inside ranges), low-overhead counter implementation (atomic ops only), and the microbench harness API for adding new scenarios.

review_conversation: Priya Nair: Could we avoid allocating strings inside NVTX scopes? I see one path in kv_cache.cpp that constructs an std::string for logging within a scope.
Ava Martinez: Good catch. I refactored that path to compute the message outside of the NVTX-scope and pass a const char*. Updated in commit e4d6b55.
Jared Thompson: The counters look fine but please add namespacing to the prometheus metric names to avoid collisions (redwood_runtime_*).
Ava Martinez: Added namespacing and updated prometheus config in observability commit c9f02a4.
Ravi Patel: The microbench harness is great. Two requests: make the default scenario deterministic and add a short local-run README.
Ava Martinez: Made default deterministic by seeding RNG and added README. Also added a small example scenario used by CI.
release_notes: Adds optional runtime telemetry: NVTX ranges, KV cache counters, batching metrics, microbench harness and a Grafana perf dashboard. Flagged behind --telemetry-enabled. Useful for diagnosing kernel and scheduling hotspots.
notes: Rollout plan: enable telemetry on benchmark-lab and a single staging cluster for 2 weeks before wider rollout. Metrics volume estimated low (atomic counters + histograms) but ingestion helper included to sample/aggregate if needed.
